paragraphs.text: SpaceX's artificial intelligence group laid off about 60 employees who worked on Grok Imagine, its image and video generation tool, over the week leading up to November 13, 2026, according to The Information. Investing.com and 24/7 Wall St. both reported the cuts based on that account, and Startup Fortune described them as more than half of the team.

Only a small group of staff remains to maintain the product, which is still available to users, according to the reports. SpaceX has not confirmed the figure, 24/7 Wall St. noted, and no statement from the company was included in the coverage.
Why the video team was cut

Management is prioritizing AI coding tools and Grok Bot, an AI agent product, according to Investing.com's summary of The Information's report. SpaceX bought the AI coding startup Cursor in August 2026 at an implied equity value of $60 billion, 24/7 Wall St. reported.

Two reasons were reported for the shift. Generating video requires more computing power than generating text, and Grok Imagine trails the leading video models in independent benchmarks, 24/7 Wall St. wrote. Investing.com added that Chinese companies such as ByteDance, Kuaishou and MiniMax treat visual models as a core priority.
The cuts mark a turn from earlier plans. In March, Elon Musk said SpaceX would double down on Grok Imagine, according to 24/7 Wall St.

SpaceX acquired Musk's xAI in February 2026 in an all-stock deal valued at $250 billion, forming the SpaceX Super Intelligence group, according to Investing.com. Startup Fortune reported that two people tied to Imagine's leadership, Haotian Liu and Guodong Zhang, had left earlier, and that xAI cut roughly 500 data annotators in September 2025.

On November 14, 2026, the Grok Imagine team announced that image and video creation now live inside Grok, the main assistant app, rather than only in a separate Imagine experience, TeslaNorth reported. The update did not include new prices, usage limits or a new Imagine model.

Grok Imagine's video model added text, image and voice references and output of up to 1080p in a July update, and the team released the first episode of an AI-made Odyssey series in October, according to TeslaNorth. OpenAI discontinued its own Sora video tool earlier this year, citing compute costs, Investing.com reported.

Read together, the reports suggest that AI video has become a hard business to fund for companies that also sell coding tools and agents. Those products are sold to businesses that pay steadily, while video generation consumes large amounts of computing power for consumer features that are harder to charge for.
The next signal is whether Grok Imagine receives any new model or feature updates in the coming months, or whether SpaceX scales it back now that most of the team behind it is gone.
